verdict: Pass. HSConfig currently reads as a narrow and competent pre-run config generator, not as HSTuner, replay analysis, winrate validation, or post-game tuning.
source_backed_claims: README.md, docs/operator/README.md, the repo skill file, the installed skill file, and CLI help all state the pre-run-only boundary.
The normal operator path is source-manifest, draft-source-documents, research-deck, prepare, validate, apply.
reports/operator_summary.json is the single operator gate.
Normal output is GlobalValues.json, Mulligan.json, per-card CardID JSON, and optional Combo.json. Presume.json and Concede.json are legacy/gated, not normal-path output.
The installed hsconfig skill is synchronized with the repo-local skill copy.
repo_evidence: python scripts/sync_installed_skill.py --check returned HSConfig skill is in sync.
Local focused verification in this audit passed 143 tests.
Subagent read-only CLI/help audit reported 85 relevant UX/scope tests passing.
no_block_implication: The UX supports the no-block promise because warnings route to inspection reports rather than to stop states. Operators should see a valid load-safe package even when semantic richness is thin.
mechanic_or_surface_gaps: Warning-only mechanics remain intentionally visible but non-blocking.
Combo detail is only emitted when concrete sequences exist.
GlobalValues keys needing runtime evidence remain outside HSConfig authority.
bloat_or_scope_risk: The main current bloat risk is documentation volume, especially untracked historical research folders.
Expert and legacy surfaces are acceptable but must stay clearly outside the normal path.
Adding replay/HDT/winrate/candidate-promotion work here would immediately make HSConfig less narrow.
recommended_next_actions: Improve validate and research-contract help text only if operator ambiguity remains.
Keep old research folders behind docs/research/current-truth.md and do not link them from the normal operator path.
Avoid adding post-game features to HSConfig.
uncertain: No real runtime apply was performed for this UX item.
Public docs were handled by the separate External Surface Sanity Check item.
